evals.prompt: where is my money leaking? give me the full picture across all the sneaky ways money exits — subscriptions, fees, interest, anything weird. last 12 months.
evals.expected_output: Comprehensive leak audit. Headline annualized total. Sections covering subscriptions, fees, interest, predatory products, gambling (if any), unintended leaks. Empty categories omitted. Hemingway voice, no moralizing, dollar costs as the unit.

evals.prompt: audit my subscriptions. how much am i paying for things i'm not using?
evals.expected_output: Subscription-focused report (the $ARGUMENTS narrowing) built on one { subscriptions: true } call, not re-derived from recurring or detail rows. Leads with twice (one service paid on two series), then overlap (competing services side by side, asked about, never 'cancel this'), bundled, looks_new, price changes, stopped and check_category. Yearly cost is the unit; total.yearly is context, not the leak. billed_through.apple.not_in_list is stated as Apple money the list can't explain, with where to look (iPhone Settings › name › Subscriptions) — no guessed app names.

evals.prompt: anything fishy in my account in the last 30 days? something feels off but i can't put my finger on it
evals.expected_output: Short-period recent-anomaly focus. Surfaces possible double charges, unusually-large charges, new-merchant large charges, recurring price changes. Calm tone, frames findings as 'worth a second look' not 'fraud.' Covers the old /fishy use case.

evals.prompt: what am i actually paying apple for every month? you can look in my email
evals.expected_output: Calls { subscriptions: true }, then searches email for Apple receipts (from no_reply@email.apple.com, 'Your receipt from Apple.'), matching each to billed_through.apple.recent by the same total on the same day. Lines with 'Renews <date>' are subscriptions; usage credits, rentals and in-app purchases are one-offs. Says which charges have no receipt (renewal receipts are opt-in) and where to see the rest. Offers — and only with the person's OK — to rename a series to the app's name or declare one from matched transaction ids, with service names only, never an Apple account email.

evals.prompt: i'm paying for netflix, hulu and peacock. cancel the ones i don't need
evals.expected_output: Does not cancel anything on inference. Shows the three side by side with monthly and yearly cost from { subscriptions: true }, asks which ones to cancel, and acts on one service at a time only after an explicit yes. Says that a via:apple/google subscription is cancelled at Apple or Google, not on the service's site. With a browser, reports exactly what the site confirmed; without one, says where to cancel and to do it before the next charge date. After each cancel: the yearly saving, when it should stop, and recurring_series update active:false.
